newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN relief team heading soon for North Korea.
newsitem.headline: UN relief team heading soon for North Korea.

text.p: A United Nations team of experts is expected to travel to flood-hit North Korea later this month to assess relief needs ahead of launching an emergency appeal for funding, a U.N. spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
Madeleine Moulin-Acevedo, spokeswoman of the U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs (DHA), told a news briefing that officials from donor countries were also to be invited.
"There is an assessment mission which should be leaving shortly for North Korea," she said. "In principle it should leave at the end of February," she later told Reuters.
"It should be composed of U.N. representatives as well as donors," she added. "This has to be confirmed."

The New York-based DHA is coordinating U.N. relief to North Korea, where floods in 1995 and 1996 left half a million people homeless out of a total 23 million and hit hard at the economy by destroying rice fields, roads, factories and livestock.

The United Nations plans to launch an inter-agency appeal for the reclusive communist state in March or April, to follow on its previous July 1996 appeal. Donors contributed roughly half of the total amount of $43.6 million sought at the time.
